questions.explain: Query Store captures query text, plans, and runtime statistics persistently across restarts and failovers, and is enabled by default on Azure SQL.
options: Extended Events, the only tuning tool available on managed services
sys.dm_exec_requests, sampled continuously
Performance Insights, because it works identically on all managed platforms
Query Store — enabled by default on Azure SQL and available on RDS and self-managed — capturing query text, plans, and runtime statistics persistently
questions.q: What is the source of truth for identifying slow queries on managed SQL Server services?

questions.explain: The query running 100,000 times a day at 50ms has more total impact than the nightly 5-minute report — tune by total impact, not average duration.
options: By average duration, descending
By total impact (total_seconds), not average duration
By execution count alone
By the number of missing-index suggestions
questions.q: In what order should the tuning backlog be prioritized?

questions.explain: The plan warning for implicit conversions turns a seek into a scan — the reading discipline is finding expensive operators by actual vs estimated rows, conversions, spills, and parameter sensitivity.
options: A missing-index suggestion from the optimizer
An outdated statistics histogram on the leading column
An implicit conversion warning that turns a seek into a scan
A parallel plan with excessive CXPACKET waits
questions.q: You read an actual execution plan and see a seek operator reading millions of rows with a warning. What is the likely cause?

questions.explain: PAGEIOLATCH_* means storage latency — the cloud storage tier is too slow or throttled. Sample waits differentially (snapshot, wait, snapshot) because cumulative counters since restart lie about the present.
options: Storage latency — the cloud storage tier is too slow or throttled; review the storage tier
A memory grant issue requiring an immediate max server memory increase
Application network slowness, since PAGEIOLATCH is a network wait
CPU saturation — the instance needs more vCores immediately
questions.q: sys.dm_os_wait_stats shows dominant PAGEIOLATCH_* waits. What does this indicate on a managed service?

questions.explain: Start MAXDOP at the core count up to 8 and raise the cost threshold from the ancient default of 5; database scoped configurations (like LEGACY_CARDINALITY_ESTIMATION) are per-database, online, and revertible.
options: Leave MAXDOP at 0 and cost threshold at 5 on all managed services
Set MAXDOP starting at the core count up to 8, and raise the cost threshold from the ancient default of 5
Set MAXDOP to 1 on every production instance to eliminate parallelism
Lower the cost threshold below 5 so more queries parallelize
questions.q: What are the recommended starting values for the two most impactful instance-level parallelism settings?
